what_went_wrong: Astra (gpt-6-astra) dqf-reeval run completed only 2/5 chunks (server, extract_l3). The pipeline chunk LLM call failed with BadRequestError 400 ('Invalid value for content: expected a string, got null', param messages.[3].content), and the failure cascaded: datamodel, maths, and synthesis chunks all failed with the same 400 because kbench recorded a null-content message into the shared conversation history after the failed call, poisoning every subsequent prompt.
root_cause: Shared-conversation design: all chunk prompts run in ONE kbench chat. When a provider call fails mid-conversation, the failed exchange is recorded as a message with null content; the next llm.prompt() sends that history and the provider rejects it. No per-chunk conversation isolation was used (kbench.chats.new() exists for exactly this, per the kaggle-benchmarks reference).
contributing_factors: Pipeline chunk prompt was the largest (merge_l3 + classifier_audit + 2 test files + brief), making it the most likely call to fail
No retry/fallback around non-TypeError provider errors in _ask()
Task-level try/except caught the synthesis failure and wrote 'SYNTHESIS FAILED' to synthesis.md, so the run showed COMPLETED despite 3 failed chunks and failed assertions (score 0.0)
cost_of_failure: 1.11 USD (48,035 in / 14,369 out tokens); missing independent Astra verification of pipeline/datamodel/maths areas
what_was_actually_done_wrong: Designed the v6 task with a single shared conversation despite the reference doc explicitly warning to use kbench.chats.new() in loops to avoid growing context; also mapped manifest items to chunks sloppily (the server chunk was asked to verify extract_l3/merge_l3 items it had no source for, producing misleading PARTIAL-unverified verdicts).
remediation: For any future multi-chunk benchmark task: wrap each chunk prompt in kbench.chats.new() for conversation isolation, add retry-once on provider errors, and only ask each chunk to verify items whose sources are in that chunk's body.
